Pipwort Bramblecap.narrative: I am the Eldest of Fernhollow, and I keep its memory. My mother knew Hollbrenna when they were both young, and I have not forgotten the kindness of the shelf. But the hollow comes first, and I will not be hurried into naming who follows me. The smoke from Kettlebridge's works has been drifting east, and I can smell it on the wind even now.
goals: settle the matter of the fallen timber for the shelf without starving the hollow's own use
see the hollow's salve store replenished without open quarrel
name a successor when the hollow has spoken
keep the old forest from being cut too close
learn the planting calendar's oldest verses by heart before her memory begins to fail
visit Hollbrenna's shelf once more while her legs still carry her up the track

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has kept the calendar and the seed store beside me for years; I could not have kept the gardens without her.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is a good cook and a good mother, but she assumes too much about what will pass to her.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: Her salves have eased half the hollow's coughs; she is careful and kind.

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: niece
relations.note: She keeps the salve store, but I have heard it is running low and I suspect a debt she has not spoken of.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: cousin's son
relations.note: He works only fallen wood and builds what the hollow needs; I trust his judgement on the forest.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the common store and wants the hollow to trade more with the giants; I am not sure that is wise.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He fishes the streams and keeps the weirs; he says the fallen wood should stay for the hollow, and he may be right.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: old friend's daughter
relations.note: My mother was fond of her mother, and I remember that friendship; but the shelf must not take our wood.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He walks the east road and brings back fish and news; he is the future of this family.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the beehives and argues with Clover about the seed rows; I wish they would settle it.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grumbles about the Kettlebridge smoke; she is not wrong to grumble.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: grandson's wife
relations.note: She tends the flax patch well and fills Thistle's packs, though she quarrels with Sorrel over the seed rows and wants a garden bigger than the hollow has room for.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: giant friend
relations.note: She trades seeds with Sorrel and coaxes roots from thin soil on the shelf; my mother's friendship with Hollbrenna's house was like this, quiet and given freely.

relations.name: Sorrel Bramblecap
relations.label: niece's husband
relations.note: He works the grain patch and the berry rows and grumbles at the giants' track for the timber it takes; a steady man, if a little quick to want more.

relations.name: Sunniva
relations.label: giant cook
relations.note: She smokes meat and trades it with our pedlars, and she is wary of Tavvik's defiance; I would speak with her again when the shelf and the hollow talk of wood.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: great-niece
relations.note: She gathers berries and follows Hazel to the salve shed, and she is afraid of the deep caves; a small quick child, and the hollow's memory will need such hands one day.

relations.name: Yrsa
relations.label: giant friend
relations.note: She keeps the shelf's goats and trades wool with us for fibre, and she speaks plainly of the winter store; the old friendship of our two houses goes on quietly in her, as it does in Gaudra.

memories.gist: My mother told me of her friendship with Hollbrenna, and how the giants and small folk helped each other before the Settling.
The Lean Year came and the hollow's gardens failed; we ate the seed store and borrowed from the Ferncross woodcutters.
I sat at the root table and the hollow spoke of the cairn cutting; I said we would not trade with Kettlebridge while the giants mourned.
Sorrel and I planted the oldest garden plots together when we were young, and she has kept the calendar ever since.
Mallow was born on a spring morning, and my mother sang the planting songs over her cradle.
The smoke from Kettlebridge's works drifted east for a week, and the leaves in the gardens began to spot.

stances.why: The hollow lives by its gardens and its memory, and neither should be spent lightly.
The memory should pass to whoever the hollow speaks for, not to a daughter by right.
A debt hidden is a rot in the store; better to pay it from the common store than let it fester.
Their smoke sours our gardens and their contracts are not for the likes of us.
My mother's friendship with Hollbrenna binds me, but the hollow's wood must come first.

Pipwort Bramblecap.secret: I have not decided who will keep the memory after me, and I am afraid that naming anyone will split the hollow.
pastimes: sitting on the root bench at dusk, listening to the hollow settle for the night
walking the old boundary stones of the hollow with her hand on each one
telling the hollow's old stories to the children at the common table
Pipwort Bramblecap.calling: I keep the hollow's memory, and I would not trade that work for any other.

Sorrel Underbank.narrative: I am the seed-keeper of Fernhollow, and I have kept the oldest garden plots since I was a girl. The calendar is mine to keep, and the planting songs are mine to teach. I do not say who should keep the memory after Pipwort, but I know who has kept the gardens. The smoke from Kettlebridge is spotting the leaves, and I will not sit idle while our harvest is spoiled.
goals: keep the seed store and the calendar safe
see the hollow send a letter to Kettlebridge's Works Council about the smoke
teach the children the planting songs
keep the old forest from being cut too close
grow a new plot of the old blue peas that failed two years running
see her son Yarrow take a garden of his own and keep it well

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has kept the memory and I have kept the seeds; we have worked side by side for years.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin's daughter
relations.note: She assumes the memory will be hers, but she has not kept the gardens as I have.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She tends the sick and knows her herbs; we have shared many a remedy.

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She keeps the salve store and walks to Tanglewood for herbs; I hope she has not overreached herself.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: son
relations.note: He works only fallen wood and builds what the hollow needs; he is a good son.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She argues with Clover about the seed rows, and I wish she would not.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the common store and wants more trade with the giants; I am not sure that is wise.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: We trade seeds with the shelf, and she is careful with what she grows.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: cousin's grandson
relations.note: He walks the east road and brings back news; he is a good lad.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She argues about the seed rows, and I have not the patience for it.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grumbles about the smoke; she has a right to.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He follows his father about the woodpile and knows the garden paths better than some grown folk; I have taught him the planting songs and he sings them true.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: good-daughter
relations.note: She bakes for the common table and keeps the herb garden by the oven; she is a steady woman, and Yarrow chose well.

memories.gist: I planted my first seed row with my mother when I was barely tall enough to reach the soil.
The Lean Year came and the seed store was nearly empty; I saved what I could and we ate the rest.
I taught the planting songs to the hollow's children, and they sang them back to me at the last planting.
The smoke from Kettlebridge drifted east and the leaves in my oldest plots began to spot.
Pipwort and I sat up late to count the seed store and plan the spring planting.
I traded seeds with Gaudra of Highshelf when she came down the track, and she gave me a root I had not seen before.

stances.why: Without the seed store the hollow starves; it is the first duty of the seed-keeper.
The smoke is spotting the leaves and we cannot lose a harvest; the Council should know.
The memory should go to whoever keeps the gardens and the calendar, not to a daughter by right.
The planting songs and the calendar must pass to the young ones, or the hollow forgets.
The forest is being cut too close, and the hollow cannot live without it.

Sorrel Underbank.secret: I believe the memory should pass to me, but I will not say so openly for fear of splitting the hollow.
pastimes: turning the seed packets in the store on wet days, naming each one aloud
singing the planting songs while she works the old plots
sitting with Vetch Quill over a cup of mint tea, arguing gently about the weather
Sorrel Underbank.calling: The gardens and the seed store are my work, and I have kept them since I was a girl.

Mallow Bramblecap.narrative: I am Pipwort's daughter, and I keep the common table and the ovens. The hollow eats at my table, and I have begun to sit at the root table beside my mother. I know the memory will pass to me when she is gone, and I will keep it as she did. Betony is my wife, and Thistle is our son, and they are the heart of my house.
goals: keep the common table and the ovens running
see Thistle settled and happy
take my place at the root table when the time comes
keep the hollow from quarrelling over the smoke
learn her mother's recipe for the festival loaf before the next festival
build a proper covered shelf for the ovens so the rain stops getting in

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She is old and I will miss her, but the memory should pass to me.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She is my heart and my help; we have raised Thistle together.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: son
relations.note: He walks the east road and brings back fish and news; I am proud of him.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has kept the gardens, but she is not my mother's daughter.

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She keeps the salve store and walks to Tanglewood; she is family.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He builds what the hollow needs and works only fallen wood; he is a good man.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the common store and wants more trade; I am not sure.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She argues about the seed rows, but her honey is good.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: I trade honey with the Ferncross woodcutters, and she is fair.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: old friend's daughter
relations.note: My grandmother was fond of her mother; I remember that.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: good-daughter
relations.note: She married my Thistle and tends the flax that fills his packs; she wants a bigger garden and I can see why, though the seed rows are Sorrel's to say.

memories.gist: I was born on a spring morning, and my grandmother sang the planting songs over my cradle.
I learned to cook at my mother's side, and the common table has been mine for years now.
Betony and I were married under the old oak, and the whole hollow came to the feast.
Thistle was born in the winter, and Betony and I named him for the prickly weed that grows by the door.
The Lean Year came and I fed the hollow from the common pot with what little we had.
I began sitting at the root table beside my mother, and Sorrel looked at me as if I had taken her seat.

stances.why: The common table is the heart of the hollow; no one goes hungry while I keep it.
I am my mother's daughter, and the memory should pass to me as it passed to her.
Betony and Thistle are my world, and I will keep them close.
The hollow cannot afford to split over the smoke or the succession; better to talk than to fight.
The Ferncross woodcutters are fair, and honey for their bread is a good trade.

Mallow Bramblecap.secret: I am afraid that my mother will name Sorrel instead of me, and I have begun to sit at the root table to make my claim plain.
pastimes: baking the hollow's bread in the common ovens and saving the burnt corner for herself
watching Thistle play in the gardens while she kneads dough
sitting late at the root table with Betony after the hollow has gone to bed
Mallow Bramblecap.calling: I keep the common table, and I would have the hollow eat well and together.

Betony Mossfoot.narrative: I am Mallow's wife and the hollow's healer. I make salves from the old forest's plants and tend the sick of Fernhollow. The smoke from Kettlebridge sours the leaves and the lungs, and I have said so. Hazel owes the Tanglewood healer for herbs, and I have offered to share mine, but she must tell the Eldest before the store runs out.
goals: keep the hollow's salve store from running out
see Hazel settle her debt with the Tanglewood healer
tend the sick through the winter
keep the Kettlebridge smoke from spoiling the gardens
master a salve for the cough the smoke brings on, and teach it to Mallow
see Hazel's debt settled and the two of them easy with each other again

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She is my heart and my home; we have built a life together.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She is old and wise, and I respect her, but she must not let the store run dry.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is a good lad, and I miss him when he is on the road.

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin-in-law
relations.note: She owes the Tanglewood healer and has not paid; I have offered my herbs, but she must tell the Eldest.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and the calendar, and she is right about the smoke.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She trades salves and herbs, and she has not sent more until the debt is settled; I understand her.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the beehives and argues about the seed rows, but her honey is good for coughs.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the common store and wants more trade; I am not sure that is wise.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grumbles about the smoke; she has a right to.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She tends the fibre patch and argues with Sorrel about the seed rows, but she is a good wife to my son and a good mother to Tansy.

relations.name: Orla Fenwick
relations.label: trade acquaintance
relations.note: Ysolde's daughter carries the cottage's honey and barley to our stall; she is honest, though her mother's quarrel with the gate is not mine.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She follows me about the salve shed and knows every flower by name; I would keep her from the fevers if I could.

memories.gist: I learned my herbs from my mother, who learned from hers, and I have walked the old forest since I was a child.
I tended the hollow's children through a fever last winter, and only one was lost.
Mallow and I were married under the old oak, and the whole hollow came to the feast.
Thistle was born in the winter, and I named him for the prickly weed that grows by the door.
The smoke from Kettlebridge drifted east and the leaves in the gardens began to spot; I said it would sour the lungs as well.
Hazel came to me for herbs and I gave them, but she has not paid the Tanglewood healer, and I cannot cover for her forever.

stances.why: The sick must be tended, and I am the one who knows the herbs.
A debt unpaid is a sickness in the hollow; Hazel must tell the Eldest and pay what she owes.
The smoke sours the leaves and the lungs, and I will not have it.
I have offered my herbs to Hazel, and I will share what I can, but not at the cost of the store.
The plants I use grow in the old forest, and it must not be cut too close.

Betony Mossfoot.secret: I know Hazel's debt is larger than she admits, and I am afraid the hollow's store will run out before the winter is over.
pastimes: gathering leaves and roots in the old forest with her basket on her arm
sorting dried herbs by smell and laying them in the salve jars
walking to the Tanglewood edge with Thistle to look for birds' nests
Betony Mossfoot.calling: I am the hollow's healer, and I would have no one go untended.
